title.narrative: Land governance support programme for sustainable management of forest ecosystems in the Democratic Republic of Congo

description.narrative:
The proposed programme intends to contribute effectively to the improvement of land tenure security of local communities and indigenous peoples, including women, vulnerable people, private actors, and access of rural populations including farmers to secure land through Land Information Systems conducive to sustainable forest management, conflict prevention and inclusive reforestation, led by more efficient and professional administrations ensuring better land governance aimed at increasing opportunities to increase agricultural productivity and restore forests (green investments) in line with national land use, land tenure and agricultural policies. In order to achieve this in a participatory approach UN-Habitat is requesting to develop a feasibility study at first to develop the programme in order to achieve the results effectively. The program is in line with the institutional reforms underway in the DRC that aim to contribute to the prosperity announced in the National Strategic Development Plan (PNSD) and the United Nations Framework for Sustainable Development (UNCSD). To achieve this, one of the pillars is the improvement of the business climate, particularly in the field of land. This requires the programme to adopt a comprehensive intervention strategy as follows:
- A mixed working approach: it will be top-down for activities related to legal and institutional reform, and bottom-up for initiatives on participatory land tenure security based on SIF tools. - The principle of subsidiarity will be respected in the delegation of missions to implementing partners by ensuring that the participatory approach is promoted at all scales of studies, construction of buildings, capacity improvement, communication, and granting of land security documents.
- The program will have six targets that will also contribute to the deployment of the process of appropriation and sustainability: the State or the national and provincial governments which will benefit from a new legislative and organizational framework of land governance, the Decentralized Territorial Entities and the customary authorities whose lands will be mapped and formalizations carried out including customary requirements, staff of land administrations and members of local land committees to benefit from training and support, households, including those headed by women and youth, who will participate in the mapping and securing processes of their land, private sector companies whose mediation and land management skills will be promoted, and national implementing agencies and providers. - Direct programme support will consist mainly of the provision of technical assistance to government institutions and local implementing agencies, the provision of grants to implementing partners and women's and youth organizations to be involved in the implementation of activities, and the payment of services to experts and expert groups. - Ownership will be based on promoting the visibility of the programme, the periodic engagement of stakeholders, and the progressive institutionalization of achievements.
The Intervention strategy will be organized around six aspects: (i) the mobilization and commitment of implementing partners and land administrations previously trained around the vision and values to be promoted, (ii) the identification and contracting of community organizations and indigenous peoples equipped with participatory mapping techniques and claims management during the planning and execution of Information System deployment activities Land (SIF) in customary lands, (iii) promoting to stakeholders plans for integrating the gender approach and communication at different territorial scales, (iv) facilitating private sector participation and identifying new (para)fiscal bases to ensure sustainability, (v) training stakeholders on the principles of engagement of CAFI, results-based management and monitoring of performance indicators, Do No Harm, and prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse in the programme cycle, and (vi) the development and joint execution of annual work and budget plans taking into account risk management. This last aspect will be the basis for the development of specific methodological frameworks that will frame the implementation and monitoring of the different dimensions of interventions: legal, regulatory, institutional and organizational reforms; deployment of land tenure security instruments; the legal review of old land concession contracts; and the participation of stakeholders, including women and youth, in local communities and indigenous peoples; and improving synergy between sectors (land, spatial planning, agriculture and forestry). The last aspect for the success of this strategy is the anticipation of the establishment of a program management team and the contracting of implementing partners to control the deadlines for carrying out the work. The program will concentrate in five years on the main phases of operation
